pairs.subject: agent-memory
pairs.evidence: crates/shadowrunr-types/src/reconcile.rs:386 Directives the agent proposed but the owner has not confirmed are stored as a `proposed`/`active: false` flag on the same `Directive` record as live standing rules, so every reader (the StreamBrief builder, list views) has to remember to filter them out. pending-beliefs-live-apart names exactly that status-column design as the failure direction that can recall an unconfirmed rule as settled.

techniques.evidence: crates/shadowrunr-types/src/reconcile.rs:386 Pending lives as a status flag on the live Directive type, not in a separate shape. Safety depends on each reader filtering on `active`.
crates/shadowrunr-types/src/reconcile.rs:446 Standing rules the Reconciler proposes from experience take effect only after explicit owner approval (human-gated).
crates/shadowrunr-types/src/memory.rs:53 Fact carries confidence, scope, sources back to episodes, and supersedes. The distilled-at time is not on the wire type, but the brain store has created_ms.
crates/shadowrunr-types/src/memory.rs:24 Type level only: each Episode carries its own observation instant. Whether the distiller grounds against it lives in shadowrunr-brain, outside this context.
crates/shadowrunr-types/src/reconcile.rs:425 Outcome credit is counted per directive from its own judge check, not copied from a whole-run verdict. An unmeasured directive is marked Unmeasured (n=0).

pairs.registryProposal: pending-beliefs-live-apart argues from read-site counts (27-56 queries). Here the live Directive list has a single named builder (StreamBrief, 'the one builder'), and the technique does not say whether a single-builder chokepoint weakens the separate-table requirement. It should say whether the rule holds regardless of read-site count.
